title: midnight-latch-and-cache-scrim-notes
content:
Context: quick overnight debug + spike to reproduce a regression in p99 tail when the coalescer and new latch code run together. We wanted a lightweight, run-in-prod-safe test so ops could roll it during low-traffic windows and we could capture traces and kernel metrics without heavy disruption.

When: 2027-03-25 23:30–01:00 (late-night scrim)
Attendees (ad-hoc): Aisha, Samir, Jordan, Maya, Ethan (on-call), + infra on standby (Kai)
Why this doc: scribbles + hypotheses + concrete action items for follow-up. Keep rough — this lives in Drive as the working log.

Observed symptom summary:
- After deploying latch-v2 (lock-free coalescer latch) alongside kv-cache-prefill change, p99 increased from ~150ms to ~320ms on small (<64 token) requests for the low-latency tier.
- CPU profiles show short, frequent spin loops at kernel scheduling boundary with ~4–8us stalls per request; aggregated they push a few percent CPU upward but spike tail.
- Traces show many requests hitting "coalesce:attempt" and then an extra codepath into latch-acquire where contention sometimes retries twice.
- Effect seems correlated with high arrival jitter (burstiness) — synthetic arrival pattern reproduction increases tail.

Repro steps we ran during scrim (keep for playbook):
1) Use traffic-replay (local harness) with arrival pattern: baseline Poisson@rps=120 -> bursty Poisson with 200ms microburst windows.
2) Deploy kernel branch with debug counters enabled (coalesce_attempts, latch_retries, backoff_ms).
3) Run 10k small-req sessions; collect p50/p95/p99, core dump of counters, and perf stat samples.
4) Collect traces via jaeger sampling rate 100% for this test window.

Quick results (sanity numbers):
- baseline (no latch-v2): p99=148ms, p95=86ms
- latch-v2 + kv-prefill: p99=322ms, p95=110ms
- latch-v2 + kv-prefill + microbatch-throttle patch (experiment A): p99=210ms, p95=95ms
- latch-v2 + kv-prefill + spin-yield tweak (experiment B): p99=174ms, p95=88ms
Notes: experiment B looks promising; experiment A reduces burst amplification but is heavier on throughput.

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: latch-v2's backoff strategy is too aggressive under high microburst jitter and spins in user-space in a way that amplifies scheduling latency.
- H2: kv-prefill introduces an extra scheduling hop that interacts with the coalescer's critical section, increasing cache-eviction pressure and causing more kernel context switching.
- H3: the coalescer's timeout heuristics cause more short-lived queues to form under bursty arrivals; combined with latch retries this multiplies stalls.

Diagnostics / observability items we added during scrim:
- counters added: coalesce_window_size, latch_attempts, latch_retries, latch_backoff_ns, kv_prefill_evictions (temporary).
- heatmap dashboard panel: arrival inter-arrival ms vs p99 contribution (new panel in console under "scrim/latch-2027-03").
- low-overhead trace span added around latch-acquire/release (span: latch.acquire, latch.release) to see retry chains.

Short-term mitigation (prod-safe):
- Roll back latch-v2 only for low-latency tier while keeping other changes (canary plan drafted: morning rollback 03/26 06:00 UTC if no fix).
- Enable experiment B (spin-yield tweak) behind feature flag and run 2-hour canary during low load.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Aisha: open a small perf PR with measured microbench for spin-yield tweak and document expected trade-offs (ETA: 2027-03-26 EOD). Linked PR: github/1914 (work in progress).
- Samir: add deterministic microburst runner to nightly bench suite and add assertion alert for p99 > 200ms on small requests (ETA: 2027-03-29).
- Jordan: expand tracing for kv-prefill codepath to include eviction hints and collect stdout samples (ETA: 2027-03-27).
- Maya: run longer 12-hour overnight canary with experiment B on a small fraction (5%) of low-latency traffic and collect metrics (ETA: start 2027-03-26 02:00 UTC).
- Ethan: update Jira INF-4821 with concrete repro steps and attach perf logs from tonight (ETA: 2027-03-26 morning).

Open questions / notes to self:
- Is latch backoff_ns tuned per-core or global? if global, it may interact badly with heterogeneous CPU boxes.
- We should simulate heterogenous boxes in bench (NVIDIA vs AMD cloud flavors differ scheduling granularity).
- Could kv-prefill be made opt-in per-model to reduce contention on hot shards? Quick thought: prefill only when seq_len>32 OR when warm-cache-hit-rate < 0.6. Need safety checks.

Ideas for longer-term fixes (brainstorm):
- Add cooperative yield points to latch acquire so long waits hand control early to scheduler instead of spinning.
- Replace latch spin loop with an MCS-style queue-free algorithm if contention remains high. (longer refactor, higher risk)
- Adaptive coalescer window: if per-shard arrival variance exceeds threshold, shrink coalesce window to reduce queue formation.
- Move small-request fast-path to a completely lock-free per-core slot to avoid global coordination for tiny tokens.

Notes about trade-offs from experiments:
- Spin-yield tweak reduces tail with minimal throughput change. But it shows slightly higher p50 in microbench due to extra syscall yield overhead in some cases. Might be acceptable for low-latency tier.
- Microbatch-throttle reduces burst amplification but sacrifices peak throughput; good as emergency throttling knob though.

Follow-up meetings:
- Quick sync with SRE + infra (Kai) at 2027-03-26 09:00 to plan canary and rollback windows.
- Design review for latch refactor 2027-04-02 (30 min) — bring microbench data.

Random scratch / todo (personal):
- paste kernel perf lines here for later: "samples: 12001, cycles: 3.2e8, stalls: 4.6e6" (grab from nightly).
- remind Maya to annotate canary results with raw span traces (not just aggregated percentiles).

Closing: tonight's scrim was useful — narrowed likely cause to latch backoff interaction with bursty arrivals. Experiment B (spin-yield) is low-risk and should be the next canary. Keep log here; will move a cleaned summary to Confluence after action items are complete.
